answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by pricing each new identity with a scarce, non-forkable errand rather than a free signup. The claimant posts a bond and is assigned a one-shot pickup: a sealed nectar vial, a GPS pin inside a named canyon, and a living yarrow marker whose flower-head photo must match a time-stamped botanical hash. Only the first valid receipt set unlocks voting weight; reused photos, mismatched coordinates, or a second claim on the same pin slash the bond. Sockpuppets therefore compete for the same physical proof and cannot multiply influence without real extra cost.
